marks.gloss_en: דכתיב: את אשר ישנו פה עמנו ... ואת אשר איננו פה
for when the serpent came upon Eve it cast contamination into her
R' Abba bar Kahana: for three generations the contamination did not cease from our fathers -- Abraham begot Ishmael, Isaac begot Esau, Jacob begot twelve tribes in whom there was no flaw at all
מאי איריא דתני גרוגרות? ליתני פירות! אלא שמע מינה בדרוסות
what forced R' Oshaya to set the mishna as R' Nechemya and as pressed [figs]? let him set it as separated [figs], and the Rabbis!
the mishna was difficult for him: why 'dried figs' and not 'fruit'? rather, pressed
Rava: the mishna was difficult for him: why does it teach 'dried figs'? let it teach 'fruit'! rather, learn from it: [it speaks of] pressed [figs]
דתניא, R' Nechemya: even a ladle, a cloak, a knife are taken only for their designated use
one baraita permits unbraiding and cutting the fig-baskets; the other forbids it
לא קשיא: this is the Rabbis, that is R' Nechemya
baraita: sealed baskets of dried figs and of dates -- one unties, unbraids and cuts
ומפורדות לא? מיתיבי, RSBG: one cuts off a wine barrel's head with a sword and sets it before guests
that [baraita] is the Rabbis; our mishna is R' Nechemya
RSBG: a person may bring a barrel of wine, cut off its head with a sword, and set it before the guests on Shabbat, and need not be concerned
מיתיבי, RSBG: one brings a barrel of wine and cuts off its head with a sword?
there he certainly intends generosity; here, if he intended generosity, let him open its opening
there [cutting off the head with a sword] -- he certainly intends generosity
the mishna: a person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, provided he does not intend to make a vessel
R' Oshaya: they taught this only of pressed [figs]
Rav Sheshet: [one who pierces a barrel with a spear] intends an opening [not, as the other side of the question had it, generosity]
ותנא קמא מאי שנא מנקב חדש ... אוסופי נמי קא מתקן פיתחא -- adding, too, fixes an opening
the first tanna: one may not pierce a new hole on Shabbat
by Torah law an opening not made to bring in and take out is not an opening; the Sages decreed because of a chicken coop, and in a coop one will not come to add, because of vermin
Rabba: by Torah law, any opening that is not made to bring in and to take out is not an opening
והיינו דקתני: לא יקבנה מצדה -- the mishna's side clause, read as the plug's side
Rav Huna: the dispute is [piercing the plug] from above
